thread:
deploy-bot: Rollout initiated: model=redwood-model-v3.2.1 -> canary group=alpha-3 (10% traffic). Artifact: weightset=ws-2026-03-17-09, tokenizer=config@v2.0.2. Triggered by CI pipeline #2981.

maria_oncall: 1min in — seeing tokenization/parsing errors from alpha-3 hosts, HTTP 502s and unfinished streams. Latency jump on the canary slice. Not yet widespread.

tom_runtime: Can you paste a couple of log lines? Which host IDs?

maria_oncall: logs (from alpha-3 host r3a-17):
```
2026-03-17T09:11:04Z r3a-17 model-infer ERROR tokenizer: unknown token id mapping at input pos 42
2026-03-17T09:11:04Z r3a-17 proxy WARN stream closed by model (partial output)
2026-03-17T09:11:05Z r3a-17 gateway ERROR downstream 502 from runtime
```

shira_ml: That tokenizer version (v2.0.2) was meant for the v3.2.0 weightset. There was a last-minute token-merge change; v3.2.1 should have used tokenizer v2.1.0. Possible mismatch from packaging.

li_sre: Incident-bot, paging: oncall-2 (li_sre) — potential impact to canary traffic.

incident-bot: Paging li_sre and maria_oncall — PRIORITY: P1 — Canary model mismatch detected. Join #incidents immediately.

maria_oncall: Confirming errors ~10s apart, ~12% of requests to alpha-3 failing with partial outputs. No customer-facing alerts yet but some trials are failing.

anya_product: We should stop routing traffic to the canary and initiate rollback/failover. Feature flag 'canary-model-routing' can be flipped to route traffic back to stable v3.2.0.

james_cs: Heads up — one enterprise customer on the trial cohort (acme-corp) may see failed responses. CS is ready to reach out if it becomes broader.

maria_oncall: I'm going to flip the canary routing flag now to stop new sessions hitting alpha-3.

ops-automation: feature-flag:update canary-model-routing -> OFF by maria_oncall at 2026-03-17T09:12:02Z :white_check_mark:

maria_oncall: Flag flipped. New sessions diverted to stable pool. Monitoring to verify traffic drain.

li_sre: Can we keep alpha-3 up for debugging but set probe-only traffic? Need memory of requests and KV caches for debugging.

shira_ml: Agreed. Do not redeploy. Lock weightset and tokenizer versions in the canary hosts for debug. Quick triage: this reads like weightset packaged with wrong tokenizer manifest — probably a CI tag mismatch.

tom_runtime: Creating emergency rollback plan: 1) stop routing, 2) mark v3.2.1 as quarantine, 3) promote fallback alias -> v3.2.0, 4) run health checks, 5) resume. I can run the alias promote now unless objections.

anya_product: Do it. Also enable verbose logging for tokenization mapping on the quarantined hosts so shira can collect more data without user impact.

maria_oncall: Alias promotion started -> promoting model-alias:latest-serving from v3.2.1 to v3.2.0.

ops-automation: alias:promote model-alias:latest-serving -> v3.2.0 by maria_oncall at 2026-03-17T09:12:45Z :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Action log updated: canary routing flag disabled, alias rolled back to v3.2.0, debugging enabled on alpha-3 hosts.

maria_oncall: Observability: error rate for alpha-3 has dropped for production traffic to baseline since flag flip. Canary hosts still show tokenizer errors (expected) but no customer impact for stable traffic.

james_cs: Notifying affected customer cohort with a short note: "We observed intermittent failures in early canary testing; we have rolled services back and are monitoring. No further action required on your side."

li_sre: Good containment. Next steps: eng-ml to do postmortem on packaging and CI tag validation, eng-runtime to add pre-deploy integration check for tokenizer/weight compatibility, SRE to add alert on tokenizer mismatch signatures.

shira_ml: I'll pull the canary artifact bundle and CI job logs — initial hunch: manifest resolution used an older tokenizer artifact due to a tag aliasing race. Will open a remediation PR to enforce explicit tokenizer sha checks.

tom_runtime: I'll add a preflight that checks tokenizer.version == weightset.expected_tokenizer before allowing canary promotion (failing fast in CI).

maria_oncall: Handing off to the next oncall for follow-up details. li_sre, please take primary on post-incident timeline + severity.

li_sre: Acknowledged. I'll draft an incident summary and severity assessment. Preliminary severity: S2 (canary-only, limited customer exposure). I'll escalate to S1 if additional customers are impacted.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0317-001. Handing to li_sre.

anya_product: Thanks everyone — please add any logs/artifacts to the incident ticket. We'll schedule a quick blameless postmortem and assign owners for fixes.

maria_oncall: Final note: customer-facing impact minimal due to quick rollback; keeping alpha-3 quarantined for debugging. Closing live mitigation.

shira_ml: I'll attach a minimal repro and the artifact diff to the incident later today.

li_sre: Closing this paging thread. If anyone notices additional anomalies ping me directly.

ops-automation: incident:update INC-2026-0317-001 status=mitigated by li_sre at 2026-03-17T09:22:45Z :white_check_mark:

maria_oncall: handoff -> next_oncall at 2026-03-17T09:23:05Z :wave:

tom_runtime: Thanks all. Follow-ups: PRs for CI preflight and alias safety, plus add automated canary kill-switch runbook.

james_cs: CS note: minor outreach performed, customers acknowledged, no escalation.

incident-bot: Thread archived.
